newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Petroz sees no divs for some time.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Petroz sees no divs for some time.

text.p: Junior oil and gas explorer Petroz NL said it was not forecasting any payment of dividends until major development decisions have been made and long-term cash flow secured.

"We are not forecasting any dividends for some time. The view of the board is a dividend will be paid when there is a sustainable and on-going profit stream," chairman, Greg Swindon told shareholders at the group's annual meeting.
Swindon also said shareholders would not be asked for any capital raising on present estimates.
"We expect current funds to last to late in 1988/89 when commitment to a development project of the Bayu-Undan field is firmed up," Swindon said.
Petroz shares were one cent lower at 78 cents at 11.40 a.m. (0140 GMT).
"For the coming year, we forecast that there will be a significant drop in operational revenue and profit related to reduced production in the Surat Basin," Swindon said in his chairman's address.
"This will result from the combination of natural field decline and competition in the market from south-west Queensland gas after early 1997," he said.
In answer to shareholder questions, Swindon said a large proportion of the funding for the Bayu-Undan project in the Timor Sea could be bank financed.
However, he said Petroz would need to go to shareholders for some of the funding in a few years time.

Swindon said he had no evidence of a takeover for Petroz from any of the Bayu-Undan participants following a potential re-alignment of interests in the field which is in the Timor Sea Zone of Co-operation between Indonesia and Australia.

Petroz has a 14.9 percent stake in ZOCA 91-12 which is exploring the Undan side of the field. Joint venture operators BHP Pteroleum Pty Ltd and Phillips Petroleum hold the adjoining ZOCA 91-13 and are exploring the Bayu side.

Swindon said a re-distribution of interests between the permits following a unitisation agreement would see Petroz having an overall interest of about 9 percent in the Bayu-Undan gas condensate field.
Petroz expected about A$25 million to A$30 million cash flow from development of the Elang and Kakautua oil fields in ZOCA 91-12 over the expected two to three-year life of the field.
Meanwhile Petroz planned to increase its exposure to potential oil-prone targets in the current year, Swindon said.
Managing director Rod Brown told the meeting Petroz had increased its interest in the Carnarvon Basin's EP325 9n Western Australia to 20 percent from four percent.

The White Opal prospect in EP325 together with the Schilling prospect in the Timor Sea's WA-74-P permit each had the potential of adding about 20 million barrels of oil reserves to Petroz's current inventory of 87 million barrels of oil equivalent, he said.
Brown said Petroz remained debt-free and with a balance sheet in good shape.
Development of the Elang and Kakatua oil fields was one of the group's priorities in the current year, Brown said.
Petroz has a 14.95 percent interest on ZOCA 91-12 which covers the two fields.
Other joint venturers are BHP Co Ltd with 42.42 percent, Santos Ltd with 21.43 percent and Indonesia's Inpex Sahul Ltd with 21.21 percent.
